title: „Ma” — choose the structure
question: The visual world is already settled: dark ground, accent-hue subject colors, tabular countdowns. This round is composition only — how the day arranges itself on a phone during a 10-minute break. The roll dealt these three.

options.label: Egy kártya
options.lineage: One thing on screen, the day as a deck you step through
options.thesis: The screen shows exactly one lesson — the one that answers the question right now — and nothing else.
options.viewport: One accent-tinted card owning the whole viewport: subject at display scale, the room number set larger than anything else on the page, the countdown beneath it, a drain bar draining along the bottom edge. A thin „Ma · 13C · szept. 1.” strip above, step dots below. Swipe or arrow to step to the next lesson.
options.case: The most reduced answer, and the one that survives being read at arm's length while walking. Every secondary fact (teacher, group, whole day) is one tap away, not on screen.
options.risk: Hides the shape of the day. A student who wants to know when they finish has to step through the deck to find out, and the moved-lesson alert has no permanent home.

options.label: Útvonal
options.lineage: The day as a journey with legs and transfers
options.thesis: Lessons are legs; the gaps between them are transfers, and the transfer is where the room change lives.
options.viewport: A single column of legs joined by a continuous rail. Each leg carries subject, time range and room; between two legs sits a transfer row reading „102 → 303 · 2. emelet · 10 perc”. Lyukasórák render as the existing acc-break hatching, sized to their real length. The running leg is lit; passed legs keep their rail but drop to hairline weight.
options.case: Takes „where do I have to go next” literally: the answer is a movement, not a location, and floor changes become visible the way a connection time is on a rail itinerary.
options.risk: Transfer rows are pure invention — Jedlikinfo gives room labels, not a building map, so „2. emelet” has to be parsed out of the room number and can be wrong.

options.label: Most + Utána
options.lineage: A live panel over a scrubbable day
options.thesis: The top of the screen answers „now”, the bottom holds the whole day as one scrubbable strip you never leave the page to read.
materials: segmented day strip in accent hues
options.viewport: Upper two-thirds: the running lesson as a large panel — subject, room, teacher, a countdown at display scale, the drain bar draining across its foot. Directly beneath, a single „Utána” row naming the next lesson and its room. Bottom: the whole day as one horizontal strip of proportional segments in subject accent hues, now marked by a live rule, tappable to preview any segment into the panel above.
options.case: Answers both questions at once — where I am now, and what shape the rest of the day has — without a scroll, and puts every control in the thumb zone. Reuses the NowRail state machine (most / szünet / mára vége / ma szabad) that already exists and is already correct.
options.risk: The most conventional of the three, and the closest to what the existing week grid already shows. It has to earn its own route rather than reading as /orarend zoomed in.
